known_facts_book1: Is one of two fat little men standing under a tree with an arm round the other's neck, the collar embroidered 'DUM'.
Says 'nohow' where his brother says 'Contrariwise', and tells Alice that if she thinks they are wax-works she ought to pay.
Insists the first thing in a visit is to say 'How d'ye do?' and shake hands, then dances a ring with Alice and his brother.
Names 'The Walrus and the Carpenter' as the longest thing his brother could repeat.
Says the Red King is dreaming about Alice and that if he woke she would go out bang, just like a candle.
Finds his nice new rattle spoilt under the tree, screams, stamps about and tears his hair over it.
Agrees to have a battle, is dressed by Alice in a bolster and a helmet that looks like a saucepan, and admits he happens to have a headache.
Proposes to fight till six and then have dinner, and boasts he hits everything within reach whether he can see it or not.
Runs off with his brother the moment the monstrous crow arrives, so the battle is never fought.

known_relations_book1.Tweedledee: His brother, hugged, contradicted and armed for a battle over the rattle that never happens.
known_relations_book1.Alice: Dances with her, has her tie on his armour, and tells her she is only a thing in the Red King's dream.
known_relations_book1.Red King: Leads Alice with his brother to where the King lies asleep and snoring.

not_in_this_book: the battle over the rattle is fought to the end
Tweedledum is killed by the crow

known_facts_book1: Is the brother whose collar is embroidered 'DEE', and who answers everything with 'Contrariwise'.
Offers the logic 'if it was so, it might be; and if it were so, it would be; but as it isn't, it ain't.'
Recites the whole of 'The Walrus and the Carpenter' instead of telling Alice the road out of the wood.
Argues that the Walrus ate more than the Carpenter by holding his handkerchief in front so the count was hidden.
Tells Alice she is only a sort of thing in the Red King's dream and that she is not real, which makes her cry.
Tries to fold himself up inside the umbrella and ends rolled up in it with only his head out, looking more like a fish than anything else.
Has a toothache on the day of the battle and a watch that says half-past four.
Runs off with his brother when the monstrous crow comes.

known_relations_book1.Tweedledum: His brother, whose spoilt rattle starts the quarrel.
known_relations_book1.Alice: Recites poetry at her, dances with her, and denies that she is real.
known_relations_book1.Red King: The sleeper whose dream he says contains Alice and both brothers alike.

not_in_this_book: Tweedledee wrote the poem about the Walrus
